page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.78-312 is an Arm-based compute instance built on the Ampere AmpereOne processor family. The server provides 156 dedicated physical cores corresponding to 156 vCPUs running at a clock frequency of 3.0 GHz. Because each core operates with a single execution thread per core, the architecture prevents simultaneous multithreading resource contention, ensuring dedicated CPU scheduling across all execution units. The system is equipped with 312.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per physical core.

The instance does not include integrated local solid-state storage and contains no discrete graphics processing units. Storage operations depend on external network-attached volumes, while workloads are restricted to CPU-based execution. Networking incorporates one complimentary public IPv4 address. Operating on the 64-bit Arm architecture (arm64), application software must be compiled natively for AArch64 to leverage the physical core pipeline without translation overhead.

With its wide physical core count and moderate memory density, VM.Standard.A2.Flex.78-312 provides cost-efficient multi-core scaling for horizontally parallel tasks. The configuration is appropriate for distributed continuous integration pipelines, containerized microservices clusters, batch data transformation, video transcoding, and large-scale web serving workloads that do not demand extensive per-thread memory or local scratch storage.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.78-312 is an enterprise compute instance powered by the 64-bit Arm-based Ampere AmpereOne architecture. It provides 156 dedicated physical cores and 156 vCPUs operating at a 3.0 GHz clock speed with a single execution thread per core, paired with 312.0 GB of system memory. This allocation establishes a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes no integrated local storage and features zero discrete GPU accelerators, requiring remote block storage for persistent filesystem needs. Network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because each dedicated core runs single-threaded, the hardware avoids hyperthreading resource contention, resulting in consistent instruction execution across massive parallel loads. This profile is engineered for highly parallelized compute-intensive workloads, including distributed continuous integration pipelines, large-scale web application serving, batch processing, and containerized microservices compiled for the AArch64 ecosystem.
